q7.answer: Workers read billing_mode from the config service and, if it is unreachable, keep the last value they read and start no new charges until they can read the flag again. The design does not say whether workers learn of a change by polling or by push, and it does not say what happens to an invoice already in progress when a forward move changes the flag. Only the rollback fence specifies how in-flight charges are handled.

q8.answer: The evidence is the rollout record in durable storage next to the ledger, which holds the gate day counters, approvals, Finance sign-off and the time the rollout entered new_only. The controller only proposes a move, a person makes it, and only the controller writes billing_mode after approval. I did not specify a hard check at the config write itself, so enforcement beyond the controller's proposal is not settled.

q9.answer: The brief sets the trigger: the new engine's charge failure rate above 2 percent over any 10-minute window, while in both or new_only. When it is met, rollback starts and further triggers are ignored until that rollback finishes. The controller runs the rollback steps, but I did not name the component that performs the detection, so that is not settled.

q10.answer: The fence stops new charges from the new engine at once, and billing_mode keeps its previous value until the final step, so the old engine does not charge either. Due charges that fail are queued for the old engine during reconciliation and stay due. The old engine makes them only after billing_mode is set to old_only, and for a rollback from new_only, only after the skipped events are replayed.

q11.answer: Before any charge, an engine checks the ledger for the charge key and skips the charge if an entry exists. The charge key is also the payment provider's idempotency key, so repeated requests count as one charge. Reconciliation also marks periods the new engine already charged as closed, and if an invoice differs from the ledger on such a period, the ledger wins and nothing is charged again.

q12.answer: The fence stays up, billing_mode stays at both or new_only, and due charges wait in the queue. The rollout record holds the current rollback step and the fence flag, so the rollback resumes from its last recorded step. billing_mode is never set to old_only before reconciliation completes, and a charge with an unknown outcome is looked up by its charge key before any retry.
